record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can randomized NC1 with read-multiple randomness, denoted BPNC1, be simulated in catalytic logspace CL?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the following complexity classes.

(1) NC^1 is the class of languages decidable by a uniform family of Boolean circuits of fan-in 2, polynomial size, and depth O(log n).

(2) BPNC^1 is the randomized version of NC^1 with two-sided bounded error and read-multiple randomness: a language L is in BPNC^1 if there is a uniform family of polynomial-size, O(log n)-depth fan-in 2 Boolean circuits {C_n(x, r)} such that the random bits r (of length poly(n)) can be read multiple times by the circuit gates, and for every input x of length n,
 - if x ∈ L, then Pr_r[C_n(x, r) = 1] ≥ 2/3,
 - if x ∉ L, then Pr_r[C_n(x, r) = 1] ≤ 1/3.

(3) Catalytic logspace CL is the class of languages decided by Turing machines equipped with an O(log n)-size read/write work tape and an additional poly(n)-size catalytic tape that is initialized with an arbitrary (adversarial) string w; the machine may read and write the catalytic tape during computation, but must restore it exactly to w upon halting. The machine must decide the language correctly for every initial content w of the catalytic tape.

Question: Prove or disprove that BPNC^1 ⊆ CL.
artifact.status_search_result: Listed as an explicit open problem in a 2024 survey on catalytic computation. Recent works (2024–2025) on catalytic logspace establish that CL contains TC^1 and admit catalytic algorithms for problems such as bipartite matching and linear matroid intersection, but no published result establishes BPNC^1 ⊆ CL. The problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Catalytic Logspace: Complexity & Applications
status_evidence.snippet: Catalytic logspace (CL) contains the circuit class TC1, which contains non-deterministic and randomized logspace (NL and BPL, respectively).
status_evidence.claim: Current known inclusions place TC^1, NL, BPL inside CL, but BPNC^1 ⊆ CL is not asserted.

status_evidence.title: Linear Matroid Intersection is in Catalytic Logspace
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results on CL include containment of matching and linear matroid intersection.
status_evidence.claim: Recent CL progress does not include BPNC^1 ⊆ CL.
